draft.title: Circadian and ultradian rhythms
card: A biological rhythm is a repeating pattern in how the body works. Rhythms are grouped by how long one cycle lasts.
a cycle of about 24 hours. The sleep-wake cycle is the main example: we feel sleepy at night and alert in the day.
a cycle shorter than 24 hours. Sleep is one example: through the night we move through NREM and REM sleep in repeating cycles.
One night of sleep holds several ultradian cycles. The sleep-wake cycle that contains them repeats about once a day.
draft.remember: Circadian is one cycle in about 24 hours. Ultradian cycles are shorter and repeat within that time.

a.q: Which description matches an ultradian rhythm?
opts: A cycle of NREM and REM sleep repeating during the night
A cycle of sleeping and waking that repeats about daily
A cycle that takes longer than 24 hours to repeat
A cycle that only occurs while a person is awake
a.why: Ultradian rhythms last less than 24 hours, and the repeating NREM and REM cycles through the night fit this. The sleep-wake cycle is tempting, but it takes about 24 hours, so it is circadian.
a.clue: Ultradian cycles are shorter than a day.

b.q: Priya sleeps from 11 pm to 7 am each night. She goes through about five NREM and REM cycles, and this pattern repeats every day. Which statement is correct?
opts: Sleep cycles are ultradian, the daily pattern is circadian
Sleep cycles are circadian, the daily pattern is ultradian
Sleep cycles and the daily pattern are both circadian
Sleep cycles and the daily pattern are both ultradian
b.why: The NREM and REM cycles each last far less than 24 hours, so they are ultradian. The sleep-wake pattern repeats about every 24 hours, so it is circadian. Reversing them is tempting because the cycles happen inside the daily pattern, but length decides the name.
b.clue: Compare the length of each cycle with 24 hours.

a.best: A cycle of NREM and REM sleep repeating during the night

b.best: Sleep cycles are ultradian, the daily pattern is circadian

problems.detail: "Sleep is one example" of an ultradian rhythm is loose. It is the NREM–REM cycle within sleep that is ultradian, while the sleep-wake cycle is circadian. Students could take 'sleep' itself to be ultradian. Better: "The NREM–REM sleep cycle is one example."

check.summary: Both questions are accurate and each has a single correct answer. One small fix: the card's line "Sleep is one example" should name the NREM–REM cycle, so students don't think sleep itself is ultradian.
